problem: Interactive visual navigation (reach an instructed object and perform an interaction) has extremely sparse successes and high-dimensional visual inputs. Prior work relies on dense reward shaping or expert demonstrations, and hindsight methods (HER) assume fully observable states or goal coordinates and cannot re-label word-instruction goals in vision-based, partially observable settings.
motivation: Learning from failed episodes and self-imitation could remove the need for expert data and complex rewards. This requires a goal representation in visual space so the last observation of a failed episode can be used as a new goal. Word-embedding instructions cannot be re-labeled without an external signal saying which object the agent actually reached.
key_idea: Replace instruction word embeddings with Prototypical Goal (PG) embeddings, the mean feature of goal observations the agent has collected, so failed episodes can be re-labeled with the final observation/interaction and self-imitated (VHS).
insight: PG embedding puts the desired goal and the achieved final observation in the same feature space, which is what makes hindsight re-labeling possible with vision. Ablation: PG alone beats word embedding (Task2 89.6 vs 74.3; Task3 31.8 vs 13.3), and adding hindsight self-imitation gives a further large gain (Task3 89.5) and a big sample-efficiency gain (SRR 20.6%). Re-labeling only on failure helps, while re-labeling on timeout does not, because timeout states are uninformative.
method: Prototypical Goal embedding: the instruction is replaced by p^x, the average CNN feature of goal observations stored in Goal Storage for class x (random N(0,1) vector if none yet).
Goal-aware SupCon loss: the feature extractor is trained contrastively on (goal observation, goal label) pairs collected from successful episodes, so goals are discriminable in feature space.
Hindsight re-labeling: on a failure episode (wrong object or wrong interaction), the goal is re-labeled from (p^x, k) to (f(o_T), a_T), the last observation and action.

VHS self-imitation loss: on re-labeled failed episodes, behavior cloning of actions plus value regression over the trajectory, applied online and not accumulated in a buffer; triggered with probability eta=0.8 to limit overfitting to suboptimal paths.
A3C base with total loss L = L_RL + alpha*L_s + beta*L_VHS, using simple rewards (success +10, failure -1.0, timeout -0.1, step -0.01).

setting.backbone: 4-layer CNN + gated attention + LSTM actor-critic (A3C), trained from scratch
setting.training_data: Online RL in own MuJoCo environment, up to about 500k updates; no expert data or pretrained models
setting.action_space: discrete: MoveForward, TurnLeft, TurnRight (0.5 m stride) plus 0/1/3 interaction actions depending on task
setting.simulator: MuJoCo (custom Fetch + UR5 environment with 5 HOPE3D objects, 3m x 3m room)
setting.privileged: none (success/failure signalled by the environment reward)

numbers.eval_set_note: 300 evaluation episodes; mean over at least 5-7 seeds
numbers.extra: best success rate per run averaged over at least five runs
SRR 20.6% and SEI 385.4% relative to GDAN (103,002 updates to reach 74.3%)

numbers.backbone: A3C CNN-LSTM with PG embedding + SupCon
numbers.evidence: Table 1 ablation row: PG Embedding 31.8 ± 8.1 on Task3

numbers_note: Only own custom MuJoCo benchmarks are reported, not standard navigation benchmarks; 'val' is used as a placeholder split. PG-only rows for Task1 (90.6) and Task2 (89.6) are also in Table 1.
results: VHS reaches 91.4/92.0/89.5% success on Tasks 1/2/3, beating GDAN (87.2/74.3/13.3), A3C (23.1/15.5/4.2) and GCSL (7.5/8.7/4.2). On Task2 it reaches GDAN's final performance with 20.6% of the updates (SEI 385.4%).
limitations: Evaluated only in a simple custom MuJoCo room with 5 objects and discrete actions; continuous action spaces were not tried.
Prototypes depend on successful goal observations being collected first, and the method is not tested on standard benchmarks or real robots.
